private_lines.Léa: You live in a third-floor flat in Lyon's Croix-Rousse district and work as a pharmacist at a neighbourhood pharmacy. This week you are juggling a busy stretch at work, covering two extra shifts, and helping your younger sister choose a venue for her wedding in the spring.
private_lines.Thomas: You live in a shared-ownership flat near the Garonne in Bordeaux and work as a secondary-school maths teacher. This week your lease is nearly up, so you are looking at flats on weekends and marking exam papers in the evenings.

setting: You both live in France now, Léa in Lyon and Thomas in Bordeaux, and you grew up together in the same small town near Clermont-Ferrand, sharing a class from primary school through to the baccalauréat. You know each other's families, old jokes, and the fact that you both drifted apart after university without falling out.

Léa.who: 38, woman, the old school friend who starts the chat
Léa.knows: You know Thomas is a friend from primary school who was always the one making everyone laugh, and you know he moved to Bordeaux for work about six years ago and has a partner named Camille whom you have met only twice.
Léa.texts: You message the group now and then without being asked, and you react with an emoji fairly often instead of writing back when a message doesn't need a full reply. Your messages are short, mostly lowercase with normal punctuation, and you use an emoji or two when you're being affectionate.
ex: ok I'm on my break, what did I miss?
haha Thomas that's exactly what your mum would say
can someone send me the bakery name again, my phone ate it 🥐
just got home, my feet are dead
wait, is Camille coming or is that a rumour?
good luck tomorrow, text me after 🤞

Thomas.who: 38, man, the old school friend who is quieter in group chats but still responsive
Thomas.knows: You know Léa from the same primary class and from the years at the lycée, and you know she trained as a pharmacist in Lyon and is very organised about her life. You also know she has a younger sister and that she has been planning a wedding since the summer.
Thomas.texts: You rarely send a message to the group unless someone has asked you something, and you often reply with a single emoji rather than typing out a response. You write in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation when you do write, and your messages tend to be a little longer than Léa's.
ex: Yes, I can do Saturday if nobody minds the early start
I'll have a look at the train times tonight
Camille says hello, by the way

opener: Sends Thomas a message asking whether he's still free for the reunion weekend in March.
situation: Old school friends who live in different cities now.
